subject: Request: Consolidate monthly invoices into annual commit (multi-year ramp options)
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Consolidating billing - moving from monthly to annual prepay

Hi Laura,

We'd like to explore switching Acme's Redwood invoicing from monthly/quarterly usage to an annual prepay model for 2026. Two key asks from procurement: a predictable price per token for budgeting, and a ramp schedule that accounts for our expected growth this year.

Our current run rate (Oct) is ~USD 42k/mo. We can commit to an annual upfront amount but need clarity on:
- discount tiers for 12-month vs 24-month commitments
- how ramp credits or phased usage will be handled in year 1 (we expect 60% of committed usage in first 6 months)
- any concessions for moving mid-contract (we're mid-November); specifically if Redwood will credit unused monthly invoices toward the annual prepay

Can you share a proposal we can take to procurement / finance? We want an SOW + PO-ready quote this month.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Ellis
Head of Platform, Acme Corp

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 12:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Consolidating billing - moving from monthly to annual prepay

Tom —

Thanks for the clear asks. High level proposal we can put into a draft SOW:

1) Term options and discounts
   - 12-month annual prepay: 12% off list rate on generation tokens; fixed unit price for 12 months
   - 24-month multi-year prepay: 18% off list rate for years 1–2 (price locked for term)

2) Phased ramp mechanics (year 1 protection)
   - Commitment is the upfront annual dollar amount. If usage in first 6 months is <= 60% of the committed tokens, we will allow a one-time temporary usage carryover (apply remaining credit to Q3–Q4) but not extend the contract term.
   - If usage materially exceeds commitment (>120%), overage pricing will apply at a blended rate (commit unit price + 20% uplift) to preserve predictability.

3) Mid-contract transition concession
   - For November/December 2025 invoices already billed, Redwood can issue a one-time credit equal to up to 50% of the unused portion of current monthly invoices when customer signs an annual prepay by Nov 20, 2025.

4) Onboarding & migration concession
   - $20k onboarding credit for account enablement (tooling + evals) on any 24-month commitment; $10k credit for 12-month.

I cc'd Ben and Marissa to validate pricing and confirm we can get DocuSign + SOW ready once you confirm which term you prefer. I can draft an SOW for either option and include the credit language.

Would Acme prefer 12 or 24 months? If you want, we can also provide a phased invoice schedule (quarterly reporting) to help with internal forecasting.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Consolidating billing - moving from monthly to annual prepay

Laura / Marissa —

Pricing confirmation for the SOW: the discounts Laura suggested are aligned with our current guidelines but two operational clarifications:

- Billing mechanics: Redwood issues the annual invoice on signature. For customers that want predictable month-level visibility, we will provide internal monthly usage reports and a quarterly reconciliation. No automatic refunds beyond credits; unused prepaid dollars remain as account credit for the term.

- Ramp protection: the "60% in first 6 months" protection is acceptable. Implementation detail: we'll model committed tokens using average unit price derived from committed dollars; carryover credits are tracked as account-level offsets.

- Mid-contract credit: 50% of unused portion is acceptable only if procurement confirms the PO is issued and full payment occurs within 30 days of DocuSign signature. This is to avoid extended receivables exposure.

- Onboarding credit: apply as invoice line item credit on first invoice post-signature.

Marissa, can you prepare the draft SOW and a Tabular quote (line items: committed spend, unit price, discount, onboarding credit, overage uplift) by EOD Wednesday so Laura can share with Acme?

Ben

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 Nov 2025 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Consolidating billing - moving from monthly to annual prepay

Laura / Ben —

Draft SOW & quote attached: Draft_SOW_Acme_Redwood.pdf (see attachments)

Quick highlights from the quote table:
- Option A (12m): Commit USD 500k prepaid annual / effective discount 12% / unit price locked through term / onboarding credit $10k
- Option B (24m): Commit USD 900k prepaid annual (years 1–2) / effective discount 18% / onboarding credit $20k
- Ramp protection clause included (60% expected first half; carryover credit language added)
- Mid-contract conversion credit clause included (50% unused monthly credit if PO & payment within 30 days)

I included example numbers based on your Oct run-rate (42k/mo): the 12m option yields ~9% annual savings vs continuing monthly at projected growth of 20% YoY; 24m locks a better unit price and gives the larger onboarding credit.

I also added a single-line note around SLA and usage reporting cadence to address procurement's predictability requirement.

If you want me to swap the billing milestones to quarterly invoices for internal visibility while still prepaying annually, I can add a sample invoice schedule.

Marissa

From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 15:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Consolidating billing - moving from monthly to annual prepay

Laura —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the clear SOW. Procurement reviewed both options. Acme is inclined to the 24-month commitment to lock the unit price and simplify forecasting, subject to the following:

1) Please confirm the 24-month total prepay amount and attach a PO-ready quote we can attach to our procurement system.
2) We will need the 50% mid-contract conversion credit spelled out exactly for November/December invoices (example numbers would help).
3) Provide the DocuSign link and the SOW with signature blocks for our legal team.

If you can get the DocuSign + finalized quote across by Nov 14 we will route PO and payment.

Best,
Tom
